en: The Method for Repentance of the Great Dhāraṇī Vidyārāja Mahāpratisarā;
the Eight Seals of Mahāpratisarā; the Eight Seals of Mahāpratisarā.
The First Seal of Repentance, also known as the Bodhicitta Seal: Turn both hands upward;
with the ring finger of the right hand, encircle the back of the middle finger.
Place the tips of the index fingers against the tips of the ring fingers;
do the same with the left hand.
Then, using the thumbs of both the right and left hands...
Twist each [finger] upon the small fingernails.
Place the tips of the middle fingers together, turn the palms upward, and hold them slightly at the heart while reciting the mantra.
Second, the Bodhi Root Seal; it is also called the Seal of the Crown of Prophecy. It is performed according to the previous seal.
Cross the two little fingers inside the palms;
press the two thumbs, left over right, each grasping its own base,
with the little fingers pressing upon the nail beds.
The index finger presses against the joint on the back of the middle finger.
This is the third mudrā, the Tathāgata Samatā-mudrā; it is also called the Śītalapradāna-mudrā. With the right hand, extend the three fingers below the index finger straight forward.
Using the thumb to press against the first joint on the back of the little finger—
this does not specify the left hand— it is the Tathāgata’s Pure Mudrā: first join the palms of both hands,
then interlace the two little fingers within the palms, with the right pressing over the left.
The head is already lowered; the three fingers are joined at the head,
and the thumbs are also joined at the head,
concealed within the palms.
The fourth is the Tathāgata Seal for Eliminating All Poisons and Evils, also known as the Seal of Universal Joy. It is based on the Seal of Equality:
interlace the wrists, with the right hand placed over the left.
The palms face upward.
If there is an external matter,
turn them outward and support it.
This is the Seal for Extinguishing Poison.

The fifth is called the Seal of All Insects Receiving the Buddha’s Prediction: first join the palms, extend the two little fingers straight upward, and bend the two ring fingers inward within the palms.
The two middle fingers are crossed within the palms, with the right pressing upon the left;
the two index fingers each hook around the two middle fingers,
and the two thumbs each grasp the side of the middle joints of the index fingers.
The two little fingers are bent together without touching the ring fingers.
This is the sixth secret mudrā, also known as the Heart Mudrā. First, join the palms and [extend] the index, ring, and little fingers.
Cross the hands back-to-back with the palms facing inward;
tuck the heads of the thumbs inside the palms,
each pressing upon the third phalanges of the fingers.
The Seventh Liberation Seal, also known as the Seal for Protecting and Mindfulness of the Ten Directions: First, join the palms at the heart.
With the index, ring, and little fingers, slightly bend them within the palms so that their nails face away from one another.
With the thumb, hide the tip [of the ring finger] inside the palm,
and press against the side of the middle joint of the ring finger.
The middle fingers are extended flat with their joints facing one another.
This is the eighth Tathāgata Heart Mudrā. First, turn the right palm upward and contemplate it with a pure mind;
then, with the thumbs, pinch the sides of the middle phalanges of the ring fingers.
The four fingers were clasped together.
The Buddha addressed the great assembly:
"For those who repent in this manner..."
All Buddhas are born from Bodhi.
When generating the bodhicitta,
one personally undertakes it without being inferior or concealing any transgressions.
It is because it is the bodhicitta itself.
Son of good family, you should know that this bodhicitta accords with the inconceivable. Why is this?
I recall that in the past, while practicing the bodhisattva path,
I accumulated merit and virtue for immeasurable kalpas,
and even passed through further immeasurable kalpas.
Practicing such asceticism for as many eons as there are grains of sand in a thousand Ganges Rivers,
he did not receive even a single prediction.
Why is this? Because the mind is inferior,
and because there remain further offenses.
Even if one were to repent and offer apologies for kalpas, one could never reach the end; because the repentance is incomplete,
calamities resulting from past transgressions will persist.
They all drew forward to create various obstacles and hindrances,
causing me to be unable to attain Buddhahood in this way; yet,
within my own mind, I earnestly sought after the Buddhas.
He made various vows. Having finished making these vows,
in a brief moment, through pure faith, he attained this seal.
This is called the Great Bodhicitta of all Buddhas.
As soon as I form this mudrā, I immediately perform repentance;
all obstacles and difficulties are instantly swept away.
The Buddhas of the ten directions have received my prediction,
that in the future I shall be named Śākyamuni,
fully endowed with the ten powers and the four fearlessnesses.
Good son, suppose sentient beings were to shed the blood of ten Buddha-bodies, a hundred Buddha-bodies,
a thousand Buddha-bodies, or ten thousand Buddha-bodies.
The blood from the bodies of hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddhas,
up to the blood from the bodies of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of immeasurable Ganges Rivers—
the blood from the bodies of Buddhas that is incalculable, beyond all calculation.
Form this seal for me.
Recite my *Prasannatā-pratisara-dhāraṇī* three times, or one time, or one phrase;
recite each name once.
It is impossible for there to be any remaining offenses that have been confessed or for any sentient beings [to remain unliberated]. Why is this?
If there were even a single remaining offense against sentient beings,
all Buddhas would lose their Bodhi. Noble son, if there is even one person who gives rise to a mind of loving-kindness and compassion, [all Buddhas would lose their Bodhi].
Bind this seal of mine and proclaim it throughout the great trichiliocosm;
let all sentient beings raise their hands in this mudrā and point toward the worlds of the ten directions.
All the karmic obstructions, illnesses, sufferings, and afflictions of all sentient beings shall be extinguished simultaneously without remainder,
and they shall immediately attain the first bhūmi.
All sentient beings likewise do not perceive it.
If one enters the palace of Māra and binds and maintains this mudrā,
the Māra King will submit in obedience and abandon his demonic activities.
If one enters a royal palace while binding and maintaining this mudrā,
one will immediately give rise to loving-kindness and patience, governing people through the True Dharma.
Should one encounter royal calamities or the like, [this shall protect them].
If one enters a province or a district and is bound in shackles,
by forming and maintaining this seal,
the shackles shall be liberated.
If the authorities themselves show leniency, both sides may attain harmony.
If a person can practice this daily,
there will be nothing in all the worlds that is not brought into accord and obedience.
The dragon kings rejoice and are able to send down rain;
all the poisonous and harmful minds in the entire world become harmonious and joyful.
If one enters into battle, [they will be victorious].
He sealed it with his finger;
the two armies reconciled, and not a single person was harmed.
"Good son, this seal of mine cannot be compared to that."
This can be understood through a single analogy:
O son of good family, even if all the devas of the ten directions were combined into ten thousand,
they would not equal the strength of a single Nārāyaṇa.
The combined strength of ten thousand Nārāyaṇas from the worlds of the ten directions does not equal the strength of a single joint of a bodhisattva.
The combined strength of ten thousand bodhisattvas from all the worlds of the ten directions likewise [does not equal the strength of a single joint of a bodhisattva].
It does not equal even the strength of a single hair-tip of the Tathāgata.
Son of good family, even if a single Buddha were able to manifest various inconceivable powers,
it would still not equal the power of immeasurable Buddhas.
Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas collectively sustain it and collectively rejoice in it.
Because it is collectively authorized;
because the Tathāgatas of the ten directions are born from it;
and because the Bodhisattvas and Vajradharas constantly provide assistance.
Because one attains enlightenment through the non-dual vision.
Good son, if one were to describe the efficacy of this mudrā, it would not be exhausted even at the end of an eon; it is inconceivable.
If there are sentient beings who wish to attain the state of Buddhahood,
they have only just attained this seal of the minor initial stage,
and they have not yet heard or known [the higher teachings].
It cannot be fully described.
The root of bodhi arises from the one mind;
it arises from the one dharma.
It arises from divergent views;
it arises from severing love and hatred;
it arises from abstaining from the karma of killing.
Born from the pure land of beginningless time;
born from certainty;
born from the straightforward and unconditioned.
It arises from gentleness and patient endurance;
it arises from courageous diligence; it arises from compassion for all sentient beings;
and it arises from great loving-kindness and compassion.
It arises from fearlessness;
it arises from hardship and suffering;
it arises from not abandoning sentient beings.
It arises from honoring and supporting one's parents and being filial and obedient to one's teachers and elders;
it arises from a mind that is not restless or agitated;
it arises from not being base.
It arises from the purification of the three karmas.
Noble son, this is the fundamental mudrā of bodhi.
Noble son, all devas, asuras, nāgas, yakṣas, the four heavenly kings, and vajrapāṇis—
The assembly of noble ones of the four fruits of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas,
as well as the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
perform these bodhisattva deeds.
That anyone could reach the end [of this path] is impossible. Why is that?
Such matters as these are the practice of all Buddhas.
Apart from the Buddhas, those who are able to perform them are themselves the inconceivable Buddha-body.
They are not bodhisattvas.
Good son, even if a bodhisattva does not hold this seal, even if they have reached the stage of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā-bhūmi), [they are not true bodhisattvas].
Nor can they receive the prediction [of enlightenment]. Why is this?
Because there is no bodhi.
Good son, if there are those who cultivate one dharma, a hundred dharmas, a thousand million dharmas, or incalculable dharmas,
yet do not maintain this seal,
they shall have no share in even a single dharma.
The assembly of sages does not rejoice in them, nor do the celestial deities protect them.
Although they may attain minor supernatural powers through the spiritual practices they cultivate,
they act in concert with the Mara King and thus do not constitute the true path.
If one holds this mudrā,
it makes no difference whether [the object] is pure or impure,
nor whether it is held or not held.
Whether making offerings or failing to make offerings,
they commit every single unwholesome deed without exception,
even within the span of a single thought-moment.
If you briefly recollect this seal and maintain it without forgetting,
at the time of death you will be reborn in the Heaven of Good Abiding and realize the King of Bodhi;
you shall also become a consecrated Golden Wheel-Turning King over the great trichiliocosm.
If one can purify the mind and body,
even if one commits evil during ten of the twelve periods of the day.
At these two times, one recollects and contemplates the Dharma and Nirvana without error or regression;
thus, in this very physical body, one realizes Bodhi.
He roams through the ten directions, no different from a Buddha.
Good son, such a mudrā is the source of all mudrās throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
If one constantly maintains this mudrā without abandoning it,
one can shake the worlds of the ten directions.
At that time, the Great Deity, the Great Yakṣa King...
The eight classes of beings, including the Bodhisattvas, Vajrapāṇis, Nāgas, and devas,
constantly come to protect [the practitioner] just as they do for the Buddha;
indeed, none other than the Tathāgata possesses such power.
Whatever they required, he would bring it himself so that there was never any lack.
Those who heard of the Buddha’s wisdom through the gateway of intelligence all understood it completely;
the wisdom of a bodhisattva is beyond description.
This seal has no original source and circulates [only now].
It must be kept secret and not spoken of rashly. Such supernatural powers and protections have already been declared to all people.
Although they see the assembly, they do not rely on others. Why is this?
Because their life-faculties are exhausted.
The supernatural powers attained are known only to oneself.
The *Hakke Hiryaku* (Secret Record of the Eight Families) states:

*Daishugyū Hachin-hō* (The Rite of the Eight Seals of Mahāpratisarā), one fascicle, by Yuigin. This was transcribed and collated on the first month of the third year of the Enpō era, the Year of the Wood-Hare (1675).
Copied to completion using a manuscript from Eshin-in, Uji, on the thirty-seventh day of the intercalary fifth month of the year of Xinchou (1201),
the year of the Vajrayāna Buddha-sons’ Pure Adornment.
In the seventh month of the year of the Rooster, during the Enpō era, at Chirinji Temple in Tōtōmi,
I had this manuscript transcribed and further collated and punctuated with *kokuji* characters.
He commanded the artisans to mount the wood.
Huī then set down his brush. Cishun.
